title: Security reports: the complete walkthrough
summary: Use every security report as a county security officer, an administrator and a platform investigator.
scenes: Choose the right scope and review access
Trace views, changes and exports in the audit log
Understand screen usage and reconstruct a session
Follow up and preserve the review trail

steps.say: We begin as Sam, a Baltimore City security officer. All people and events in this video are synthetic training examples.
Security officers review users, sign-ins, audit events and usage within their granted places. This role does not provide patient records or account editing.
onScreen: People who work for, or have access to, the tenants you review. Read only: ask an administrator to change an account.

steps.say: Check the active profile and working place before reviewing. A narrower profile narrows your reports; regional and platform administrators can cover several data roots.

steps.say: Export users and access for an access review. The export uses your permitted scope; the filter box only filters the on-screen list.
Ask an administrator to correct unexpected access or an account problem. The security officer reviews evidence without changing accounts.
Open Sign-in activity from Administration to investigate suspicious patterns. These are leads to check, not proof that an account was compromised.
Choose a window: one hour, one day, seven days or thirty days. Show refreshes the report for that window.
One address trying five or more accounts or unknown names suggests password spraying. Compare the target count, failures and first and last times.

steps.say: None means no matching pattern in this period and scope. It does not prove there were no attempts elsewhere or outside the selected window.
Export this report downloads every report section for the selected window. Section names identify the pattern represented by each CSV row.
Open Audit log for the tamper-evident history of views, changes and exports. It records actions and identifiers, rather than copies of free-text record contents.
onScreen: Events 1–100 of 197, newest first.

steps.say: Choose Sign-in and account security (all), then Search, to see security actions together instead of choosing one action at a time.
actions: Chooses “Sign-in and account security (all)” for Action

steps.say: Clear filters to return to the whole ledger. Combine User, Action, Record type and dates to answer who did what and when.

steps.say: For example, find Sam's access-review exports. Choose Sam under User, Exported under Action, and Users and access under Record type.
actions: Chooses “Users and access” for Record type

steps.say: Set From and To for the review period, then Search. The count confirms whether your combined filters found events.
For one record, use Record id or its all events link. A record link opens the record only when your permissions allow it.
actions: Selects “Every event for this record (all events)”

steps.say: Events are newest first. Choose twenty-five or one hundred per page; use the page links to review older events when more exist.
Download CSV preserves the current filters, with at most the newest ten thousand events. Narrow the dates if you need a smaller review set.
County review includes scoped staff and events on records owned there when logged. Older events without an owner stamp rely on staff scope.
onScreen: Events 1–100 of 198, newest first.

steps.say: Open Usage to review screen visits and navigation. Choose one, seven, thirty or ninety days, then Show usage.
Visits by screen compares visits, sessions and timed visits. Visible time is optional, capped focused time; missing time means unknown.

steps.say: Expand Visits by active-profile role for role totals. One visit can have several roles, so adding role counts together would double-count visits.
Paths into Enter a result shows up to three preceding screens. Back-and-forth paths can be useful review, not necessarily mistakes.

steps.say: Download this page CSV exports the current page, up to one hundred visits. Use session paging for additional visits.
You can also paste a session reference into Open a session reference. The reference is a reporting identifier, not a sign-in credential.

steps.say: No retained events or no visits can reflect scope, period, missing telemetry or retention. Browser closure alone does not prove that someone signed out.
We now switch to the Maryland administrator. Administrators can open account pages and act on problems that a security officer reports.
Filter for Security Training Staff 1 and open the account. Review the master profile to check places, roles, access levels and grant dates.
Sign-in history shows the latest fifty events: time, event, reason, address, browser and shortened session and attempt references.

steps.say: Export this account's sign-in history downloads up to one thousand events. Keep the account history with the activity and audit exports for your review.
We now switch to the platform administrator. Unknown user names belong to no county, so they require the security investigation permission.
Open Unknown user names. Hashes group repeated attempts at the same name without revealing what someone typed.

steps.say: Export the hashed list saves hashes and counts. The typed names are never included in this export.
Use Show names only when the investigation needs it. A name may contain a password entered in the wrong box; do not copy or share the revealed text.
onScreen: Names may occasionally include a password someone typed into the user-name box by mistake. Showing names is recorded in the audit log. Use them for this investigation only; don't copy them out of this page or share them.

steps.say: Enter a current authenticator code, then Show names. The code stays masked in this video, and the reveal is recorded in the audit log.
Names are revealed for this page only. If an encryption key is no longer available, a name can instead appear as no longer readable.

steps.say: Return to Unknown user names to restore the hashed view. This ends the temporary on-page reveal.
Finally, open Audit log and filter Action to Export. Report exports, unknown-name lookups and reveals leave an audit trail of the investigation itself.
Use the report that matches the question: access for permissions, sign-ins for authentication, audit for recorded actions, and usage for observed navigation.
Record the scope, time window, affected account or session, and your findings. Refer account and grant changes to an authorized administrator.
